title: How your eyes see
examples: How does light get from the object to my eye?
What part of the eye focuses the light?
Why do I need to blink my eyes?

explain.say: The cornea is the clear outer window at the front of your eye.

draw.text: Cornea: Outer window of the eye.

explain.say: Next, the lens works like a camera lens to focus light onto the back.
The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the very back of your eye.
Your retina has two types of cells, rods and cones, to see things.
When light hits the retina, the brain receives signals that are upside down.
In real life, when you look at a book, the light bounces off the words to your eye.

faq.q: What is the main job of the retina?
faq.a: The retina contains special cells called rods and cones that detect light. These cells convert light energy into electrical signals for the brain.
asks: What happens at the back of the eye?

faq.q: Why does my brain flip the image?
faq.a: The eye naturally receives an upside-down image. The brain automatically processes and flips it so you see the world correctly.
asks: Is the image upside down in my eye?
How do I see right-side up?

faq.q: What is the difference between rods and cones?
faq.a: Rods help you see in very dim light, like at night. Cones allow you to see colours and fine details in bright light.
asks: What helps me see in the dark?

faq.q: Does the cornea do all the focusing?
faq.a: No, the cornea starts the focusing, but the lens fine-tunes it to make the light sharp on the retina.
asks: Is the cornea the only focusing part?

faq.q: How does the light travel through my eye?
faq.a: Light enters through the cornea, passes through the pupil, is focused by the lens, and finally hits the retina.
asks: What is the path of light?
What is the order of the eye parts?

facts: The cornea is the transparent front part of the eye.
The lens changes shape to focus light onto the retina.
Rods are responsible for vision in low light conditions.
The brain interprets the signals from the retina correctly.

quiz.say: Light passes through the cornea and is focused by which structure before reaching the light-sensitive layer?
quiz.why: The lens adjusts its shape to fine-tune the focus of light coming through the cornea.

wrong.0: The cornea is the entry window, but the lens does the main focusing work.
wrong.1: The retina is the screen at the back; it receives the focused light, it does not focus it.
wrong.2: The pupil is just the opening that controls how much light gets in.

quiz.say: If you are in a very dark room, which type of cell in the retina helps you see shapes?
quiz.why: Rods are specialized for detecting light when there are very few photons available.

wrong.0: The cornea is a physical part, not a light-detecting cell type.
wrong.1: The lens focuses light, but the rods are the cells that detect the low light.
wrong.3: Cones need brighter light to work properly and see colours.

quiz.say: When you look at a picture, the image you see is:
quiz.why: The brain automatically flips the image so that you perceive the world as correctly oriented.

wrong.0: This describes poor vision, not the brain's processing of the image.
wrong.2: The image hitting the retina is upside down, but the brain corrects this.
wrong.3: While the image is reversed, the brain corrects this too, so you don't see a mirror image.
